_comment: TEMPLATE for the chore list. Copy to db/chores.json (gitignored, like household.sql) and
edit. Apply with:  npm run provision -- --chores db/chores.json
It is ADDITIVE and never deletes: only the ids named here are touched, a chore absent from
the file is left exactly as it is, and retiring is `active = 0` rather than a DELETE - so a
truncated file cannot empty the board and cannot orphan the ledger rows that record work a
child actually did and was paid for. Re-running it is safe.
THE ONE RULE THE CODE DOES NOT ENFORCE: `kind` decides which DESTINATION the tile appears
under; `basePoints` decides what it PAYS. Nothing stops a duty from paying. If the house
rule is 'duties are expected and pay nothing, extras are chosen and earn money', that rule
lives HERE, in the data - give every duty basePoints 0. A zero-point chore is legal and
writes no ledger row at all, so it runs the full state machine and moves no money.
The chores in the live database as of 2026-08-29 are still mostly the DEV SEED from
db/seed.dev.sql - ch-table, ch-tidy, ch-bed, plus an authored ch-clear. One per
assignment model, all duties, all paying, i.e. a fixture rather than a household list.
To switch the board over, put their ids in `retire` in the SAME run that adds the real
ones. `retire` is left empty here on purpose: the writer refuses the whole file if it
names an id that does not exist, so a pre-filled list would make this template fail on
any database but one. Retiring is `active = 0`, never a DELETE, and `restore` undoes it.
PETS: a chore with category "pet" and kind "extra" is one of the pet's own asks, and
shows on the pet's sheet as well as the board - but only when the household has a pet
(`pets` in db/household.json, applied with --settings). With `pets: []`, the default, there
is no sheet and such a chore is an ordinary extra on the board; keep it, rename it or retire it.
REMINDERS: a duty may carry "countsTowardDay": false. It stays on the board, is claimed and
pays exactly as before, but it does not count toward a FULL DAY (ADR-0006 s4): done or not, it
leaves the day. Use it for a duty that is not really asked every day, such as homework on a
school night with none. Omitted means true for a duty; an extra never counts, and
"countsTowardDay": true on an extra is refused. Re-applying the file wins over the wall.

chores._note: DUTY, individual: each child gets their own tile. basePoints 0 = expected, unpaid.
DUTY, scoped to two children by listing them in `rotation` - it doubles as a roster.
EXTRA, first_complete: whoever claims it first earns it; the others go `superseded`, which is neither a win nor a miss and never breaks a streak (ADR-0005).
EXTRA, rotation: `rotation` is the ORDER, and it advances one child per occurrence.
EXTRA, shared: everyone listed gets a tile and each is claimed and paid separately.
